probes.interpretation: Executed with Python 3.13.12. Compatibility probes simulate missing older-interpreter APIs; no claim of actual Python 3.10/3.11 execution.

findings.issue: Directory enumeration allocates the entire directory before enforcing prospective capacity
findings.evidence: Inspected installed Python 3.13.12 Path.iterdir: it creates [entry.path for entry in scandir_it] before returning. The in-memory probe with artifact_records=1 consumed all four entries before Package enumeration exceeds limits.
findings.impact: Both fixed-package walkers can allocate an arbitrarily large directory listing before their counter/work/text limits reject it. Existing memory filesystem tests do not exercise this eager native adapter behavior.
findings.repair: Use a streaming directory metadata boundary and charge each entry before retaining child paths; preserve fixed roots, exact names, link rejection and fail-closed unsupported resource behavior. Test consumption stops at the first excess entry through an in-memory scanner. Correct the associated prospective-bounding docstrings as part of the behavior repair.

findings.issue: Unconditional tomllib import breaks the declared Python 3.10 build/test path
findings.evidence: Root and runtime pyproject declare >=3.10,<4.0; CI includes 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13. tomllib was added in 3.11. The simulated missing-module probe raises ModuleNotFoundError while importing the helper.
findings.impact: Python 3.10 cannot import the builder or collect the dependent builder tests. Python 3.11 has tomllib and reaches the separate path API defect.
findings.repair: Use an already-approved repository-compatible TOML parser or compatibility import without silently increasing the minimum Python version or adding an unapproved dependency. Keep byte/syntax/depth validation and immutable metadata projection. No broader parser inventory was performed.

findings.issue: Older supported Python versions either crash on junction checks or omit junction rejection
findings.evidence: Path.is_junction was added in 3.12. A Path-shaped 3.11 API probe raises AttributeError at the build root. With runtime version_info=(3,11), is_symlink=False and is_junction=True, _linked returns False. Existing junction test requires rejection unconditionally.
findings.impact: On 3.10/3.11 the build helper fails on ordinary directories after import succeeds; runtime reads may follow Windows junctions because rejection is disabled. Existing junction test also fails under those versions. On 3.12/3.13 the API exists, but the eager enumeration defect remains.
findings.repair: Use a Python-3.10-compatible non-following metadata check for Windows reparse points/junctions and symlinks, consistently for build/runtime roots, ancestors and members. Do not repair compatibility by suppressing junction checks or weakening the test. Keep metadata failure fail-closed and add in-memory old-version coverage.
